dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Dunn introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Ways and Means, and in addition to the Committee on Financial Services, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to provide for a credit against tax for homebuyers purchasing residences in residential recovery zones, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Residential Recovery Zone Act.

subsection.text: Subpart A of part IV of subchapter A of chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting after section 25D the following new section:

paragraph.text: In the case of an individual who purchases a principal residence in a residential recovery zone during a taxable year, there shall be allowed as a credit against the tax imposed by this subtitle for such taxable year an amount equal to 10 percent of the purchase price of the residence.
At the election of an individual, the credit allowed under subsection (a) for a taxable year may be allowed instead during any one on the subsequent 3 taxable years.

subparagraph.text: Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph, the credit allowed under subsection (a) shall not exceed $8,000.
In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, subparagraph (A) shall be applied by substituting $4,000 for $8,000.

If two or more individuals who are not married purchase a principal residence, the amount of the credit allowed under subsection (a) shall be allocated among such individuals in such manner as the Secretary may prescribe, except that the total amount of the credits allowed to all such individuals shall not exceed $8,000.

paragraph.text: No credit shall be allowed under subsection (a) for the purchase of any residence if the purchase price of such residence exceeds $1,500,000.

subparagraph.text: The term residential recovery zone means, with respect to a Federally declared disaster, a population census tract that is—

clause.text: in the disaster area related to such disaster, and

subparagraph.text: A population census tract is designated under this paragraph with respect to a Federally declared disaster if, during the period beginning on the earliest incident date specified in the declaration to which such area relates and ending on the date that is one year after such date—

clause.text: the chief executive officer of the State in which the tract is located—

subclause.text: nominates the tract for designation as a residential recovery zone, and
notifies the Secretary in writing of such nomination, and

clause.text: the Secretary certifies such nomination and designates such tract as a residential recovery zone.

subparagraph.text: A designation under subparagraph (B) shall terminate on the date that is 3 years after the date of the certification described in subparagraph (B)(ii).

subparagraph.header: State; Federally declared disaster; disaster area
subparagraph.text: The term State has the meaning given such terms in section 1400Z–1, and Federally declared disaster and disaster area have the meaning given such terms in section 165(i).

paragraph.text: The term principal residence has the same meaning as when used in section 121.
The term purchase and purchase price have the meanings given such terms in section 36(c).

subsection.text: No credit under subsection (a) shall be allowed to any taxpayer for any taxable year with respect to the purchase of a residence if—

paragraph.text: a deduction under section 151 with respect to such taxpayer is allowable to another taxpayer for such taxable year, or
the taxpayer fails to attach to the return of tax for such taxable year a properly executed copy of the settlement statement used to complete such purchase.

If a residence with respect to which a credit was allowed under subsection (a) ceases to be the principal residence of the taxpayer before the end of the 3-year period beginning on the date of the purchase of such residence the tax imposed by this chapter for the taxable year of cessation shall be increased by the amount of the credit so allowed and claimed.

subparagraph.text: Paragraph (1) shall not apply if the cessation is attributable to the taxpayer’s death.

Paragraph (1) shall not apply if the cessation is attributable to a compulsorily or involuntarily conversion (within the meaning of section 1033(a)) and the taxpayer acquires a new principal residence during the 2-year period beginning on the date of such cessation.

subparagraph.header: Special rule for members of the armed forces, etc

clause.text: Paragraph (1) shall not apply if the cessation is attributable to Government orders received by such individual, or such individual’s spouse, for service on qualified official extended duty as—

subclause.text: a member of the uniformed services,
a member of the Foreign Service of the United States, or
an employee of the intelligence community.

clause.text: Any term used in this subparagraph which is also used in section 121(d)(9) shall have the same meaning as when used in such paragraph.

subsection.text: The table of sections for subpart A of part IV of subchapter A of chapter 1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 25D the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: Sec. 25E. Residential recovery zone homebuyer credit.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply with respect to purchases in taxable years beginning after the date that is 1 year before the date of the enactment of this Act.
Section 1400Z–1 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

paragraph.text: With respect to a Federally declared disaster, the chief executive officer of a State may designate under this paragraph not more than 5 percent of the applicable disaster tracts in such State with respect to such disaster.

paragraph.header: No effect on limitation on number of designations
paragraph.text: An applicable disaster tract designated under paragraph (1) shall not be taken into account in determining the limitation under subsection (d).
The term applicable disaster tract means, with respect to a Federally declared disaster, a population census tract in the disaster area related to such disaster.
In this subsection, the term Federally declared disaster and the term disaster area have the meaning given such terms in section 165(i).

subparagraph.header: Qualified opportunity fund businesses and property
subparagraph.text: In the case of an applicable disaster tract designated under paragraph (1), subparagraphs (B)(i)(I), (C)(i), and (D)(i)(I) of section 1400Z–2(d)(2) shall each be applied by substituting the applicable start date for December 31, 2017.

In the case of an applicable disaster tract designated under paragraph (1), section (c)(2)(B) shall be applied by substituting the applicable start date for the date of the enactment of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.
The term applicable start date means, with respect to a disaster area, the earliest incident date specified in the declaration to which such area relates.

subsection.text: The amendments made by this section shall apply with respect to Federally declared disasters declared after the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.header: Credit under the Community Reinvestment Act of 1977 for lending in a residential recovery zone
section.text: Section 804 of the Community Reinvestment Act of 1977 (12 U.S.C. 2903) is amended by adding at the end the following:

subsection.text: In assessing and taking into account, under subsection (a), the record of a financial institution, the appropriate Federal financial supervisory agency shall consider as a factor lending activities to individuals and businesses that are located in a residential recovery zone (as defined under section 36A(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986).
